findings.claim: O3 removes the whole `kmctl audit` group, including `kmctl audit guard`, but the shipped agents call it from their PreToolUse hooks (`command: "kmctl audit guard --allow checks"` in kmctl-check-writer.md, the same with `claims` in kmctl-claims-extractor.md), and guard.py only lets through commands that start with `kmctl audit GROUP`. The hook, guard prefix, agent text and skill commands only work if they change together with the removal. The facts split them up: the agent and skill files sit in O4 (`support`, needs O3) while tests/test_apm_package.py, which asserts the exact hook command, sits in O3. If plan.split ships O3 without O4, either O3's gate fails (the test's new assertion does not match the agent files) or, if the test is left alone, the agents' hooks call a missing command and Claude Code blocks every shell call the agents make. O1 has the same tie: the guard's allowed prefix moves to `kmaudit GROUP` in the moved guard.py, which only fits agents that say `kmaudit`. Fix: put the agent hook commands, the agent and skill command text and the test_apm_package.py assertion in one outcome with the removal (O3), or make O3 behaviour-coupled so it cannot ship without them. Leave only docs, README, .okf and the ADR in O4.

r6 and O4's check (no `kmctl audit` outside .loop/, .okf/log.md, .okf/prototypes/ and decision records the new one supersedes) catch more than O4's touches list, and some of it should not be rewritten. Ten accepted records that the new record does not supersede (0001, 0009, 0012, 0014, 0015, 0017, 0018, 0021, 0022, 0034) each end with the history note "Found by the first `kmctl audit checks` run over the whole bundle". action.yml:160 and docs/how-to/install-the-plugin-and-the-ci-action.md:473 print "kmctl audit: refused for event ...", the error prefix of the Action's own audit mode, which is not the moved audit at all. Also outside O4's touches: apm/.apm/skills/{extract-claims,write-checks}/evals/{evals.json,results.md}, .okf/architecture/index.md and .okf/decisions/index.md. As signed, r6 makes the build either rewrite true history in records that were not superseded and reword an unrelated Action message, or fail the row. Decide what the exclusions should be (for example, all decision records' history notes, or only commands a user would run) and list the files that really change in O4's touches, so plan.split and the eval agree with the prose.
The removal of `kmctl audit` and the agent hook, guard prefix and skill commands that call it were split across outcomes that could not ship apart.
r6's grep caught history notes in accepted decision records and the Action's own audit-mode refusal, and O4's touches missed files r6 forced to change.
